title: CompTIA Linux+ (XK0-005)
summary: CompTIA Linux+ (XK0-005) is a vendor certification offered by CompTIA. This independent study guide covers all 5 objective domains: System Management, Services and User Management, Security, Automation, Orchestration, and Scripting, Troubleshooting. Each domain is broken into 29 lessons in total, and every lesson has a MEDIUM and a HARD scenario exam. The exams use realistic workplace situations rather than recall questions, so you practise applying each objective the way the job asks for it.
attributionNote: CompTIA certification content is an independent study guide written for Cyber Pulse Academy and is not affiliated with or endorsed by CompTIA.

beginner.definition: This is a professional certificate from CompTIA about Linux. Linux is the family of open source operating systems used on most servers. It is an intermediate exam, which means it expects real practice at a text command line. The exam code is XK0-005, and some questions ask you to complete a task.
beginner.whyItMatters: Web servers, cloud platforms and network appliances mostly run Linux. Companies need people who can keep those machines secure and working. This certificate shows you can do that work by hand, without a mouse or a control panel. It fits help desk staff who want to move up, and it supports later cloud and security certifications. Employers often treat it as proof of practical skill rather than theory.
howItWorks: Install Linux on a spare computer or a virtual machine, because you learn more when you can break it.
Practise the everyday tasks, such as creating users, setting permissions, mounting storage and managing services.
Learn a scripting language, because automation is a large part of the job and of the exam.
Study security topics such as file permissions, firewalls and mandatory access control, and apply them on your own host.
Practise troubleshooting by breaking something on purpose and reading the log files to find the cause.
Take practice tests, then sit the proctored exam, which includes task based items in a simulated system.
beginner.example: Picture a shared office kitchen with a locked cupboard. Every colleague needs a key for the cupboard. Only the manager should change who holds one. If the keys are copied carelessly, anyone can take the expensive coffee machine. On a Linux server the same idea appears as file permissions and user groups. Each file states who may read, write or run it. A Linux administrator decides who gets which key.
takeaways: You cannot pass this exam by reading alone, because several questions require practical actions.
Learn the command line slowly and correctly, because small typing errors cause real outages.
Confirm the current exam version and objectives on the CompTIA website before you book a date.
